abort.configuration_changed: The saved configuration changed while this form was open. Reopen Reconfigure to work from the current configuration.
abort.one_mapping_required: This integration needs at least one thermostat mapping. Keep one mapping, or remove the integration entry to remove them all.
abort.invalid_datapoint_identity: This datapoint identity is missing or repeated in the saved configuration. No changes were saved. Restore one distinct stable identity per datapoint before editing.
abort.datapoint_source_limit: This saved datapoint has more than three sources. This form supports up to three and cannot edit it without losing sources. No changes were saved.
abort.datapoint_not_supported: This saved datapoint uses a contract that this form cannot edit. No changes were saved; retain its configuration until a compatible form is available.
abort.historical_identity_invalid: This saved daily history mapping has a missing or repeated stable identity. No changes were saved. Restore one distinct identity per mapping before editing.
abort.historical_source_limit: This saved daily history mapping has more than three sources. This form supports up to three and cannot edit it without losing sources. No changes were saved.
abort.historical_not_supported: This saved daily history mapping uses a contract that this form cannot edit. No changes were saved; retain its configuration until a compatible form is available.

error.duplicate_mapping_name: Another mapping has this name, ignoring surrounding spaces and letter case. Enter a distinct name.
error.duplicate_optional_source: An optional entity was selected more than once. Assign each optional entity to one role in one thermostat mapping.
error.duplicate_homekit_source: This HomeKit climate is already assigned to another mapping. Select the HomeKit climate for a different thermostat.
error.homekit_device_required: The HomeKit entity has no existing Home Assistant device association. Restore that association in HomeKit Device, then select the entity again.

error.invalid_name: Enter a mapping name containing 1–64 characters after surrounding spaces are removed.

error.invalid_datapoint_id: The datapoint needs a distinct stable identity. Reopen Reconfigure before continuing.
error.invalid_datapoint_name: Enter a datapoint name containing 1–64 characters after surrounding spaces are removed.
error.invalid_datapoint_kind: Choose one of the supported quantity types.
error.invalid_source_count: Select two or three sources for this datapoint.

error.invalid_interval: Enter a positive whole-number interval length in seconds.
error.invalid_max_age: Enter a whole-number maximum report age of zero or more seconds.
error.invalid_fallback: Choose whether fallback to the other selected sources is allowed.
error.invalid_semantic: Choose the quantity meaning that all selected sources actually represent.
error.invalid_unit: Choose a supported unit for this quantity; use the exact Home Assistant unit spelling.
error.unexpected_interval: Clear the interval length for a current observation datapoint.
error.unexpected_unit: Clear the unit for a quantity that does not use numeric units.

error.temperature_semantic_required: Choose physical temperature or control temperature for a temperature datapoint.
error.source_missing: A selected source is missing or disabled. Restore it or select an existing enabled entity.
error.source_attribute_missing: A selected attribute is not present on its source. Check the exact attribute name.

error.unsupported_source_platform: Select sources from HomeKit Device, Ecobee, Beestat Statistics, or Battery Notes with proven Ecobee device identity.

error.invalid_text: The selected text value must be nonblank and at most 255 characters.

error.invalid_number: The selected source must report a finite numeric value.
error.invalid_temperature: The selected temperature must be finite and no lower than absolute zero.
error.invalid_percentage: The selected humidity or battery value must be between 0 and 100 percent.
error.invalid_duration: The selected duration must be finite and zero or greater.
error.invalid_timestamp: Use a source timestamp with a date, time and explicit time zone.

error.weather_source_duplicate: Select distinct weather entities for the ordered sources.
error.weather_station_unknown: The weather source does not identify its provider station. Wait for a complete source report.
error.weather_station_mismatch: The weather sources report different stations. Select aliases of the same feed. A changed station requires a new datapoint.
error.weather_config_entry_mismatch: The weather sources must use the same Ecobee account connection.
error.weather_device_identity_mismatch: The native weather entity no longer matches its source thermostat device. Restore the source association.
error.weather_attribution_invalid: The native weather attribution does not contain a supported station and provider timestamp.
error.weather_timestamp_invalid: The native weather provider timestamp is invalid. Restore the source report.
error.weather_timestamp_future: The weather provider timestamp is more than one minute in the future. Check its source clock.
error.weather_unit_invalid: A native weather unit is missing or unsupported for this quantity.
error.weather_unit_mismatch: The selected output or declared source unit does not match a supported weather conversion.
error.weather_value_invalid: A selected weather value is invalid for its quantity.
error.weather_value_missing: The selected current weather field is missing. Choose a supplied field or wait for source recovery.
error.invalid_weather_role: Select the same supported weather field in every source. Whole weather mappings need blank attribute, unit, and timestamp fields.
error.membership_profile_context_missing: The member list is missing its associated comfort-profile context. Select a source that reports the list and profile together.

error.historical_quantity_invalid: Choose temperature, relative humidity, battery level, carbon dioxide, air quality index, VOC, weather temperature, or weather humidity.

user.description: Create a unified climate for each thermostat already present in both HomeKit Device and Ecobee. Add optional sources for presets, Clear Hold, precise temperature, air quality, or thermostat messages.

data_description.add_another: Continue to another thermostat after accepting this mapping. The integration entry is created when you submit a mapping with this option cleared.
data_description.ecobee_aqi_entity: Display the existing index from this thermostat’s Ecobee sensor. The source must have aqi device class, no unit, and a nonnegative numeric reading when available. Ecobee Unified supplies no separate index calculation.
data_description.ecobee_co2_entity: Add carbon dioxide reported by this thermostat’s Ecobee sensor. The source must have carbon_dioxide device class, ppm units, and a nonnegative numeric reading when available. A valid sensor contract does not establish whether Ecobee measured or estimated the value.
data_description.ecobee_entity: Select the same thermostat’s climate entity from Ecobee. It supplies vendor status, observes most normal control requests, and handles Ecobee-specific actions. Its usable readings can fill gaps without enabling cloud control of normal thermostat functions.
data_description.ecobee_notify_entity: Select the notification entity on the same Ecobee thermostat. The unified notify entity forwards the message body for display; titles are ignored. Delivery is unconfirmed and does not create or replace a thermostat command status.
data_description.ecobee_voc_entity: Add VOC concentration reported by this thermostat’s Ecobee sensor. The source must have volatile_organic_compounds device class, µg/m³ units, and a nonnegative numeric reading when available. A valid sensor contract does not establish whether Ecobee measured or estimated the value.
data_description.homekit_clear_hold_entity: Select the actual Clear Hold button on the same HomeKit thermostat. Metadata checks reject known incompatible roles but cannot prove a generic button’s purpose. Resume program presses this button once and records submission; it cannot verify which schedule resumes.
data_description.homekit_entity: Select the thermostat’s climate entity from HomeKit Device. This entity supplies local readings and determines which normal thermostat controls are available.
data_description.homekit_preset_entity: Select Current Mode on the same HomeKit thermostat. Its advertised home, sleep, or away options become local preset controls. A matching report from this select confirms a preset request; an unknown current value can still leave valid options usable.
data_description.homekit_temperature_entity: Select the thermostat’s own HomeKit temperature sensor with temperature device class and °C, °F, or K units. Its converted reading supplies extra precision only while agreement and recovery checks against the local climate pass. Receiving reports alone does not establish a new physical measurement.
data_description.name: Give this thermostat a distinct name, up to 64 characters. Renaming a mapping retains its existing identity.

mapping.description: Pair the HomeKit and Ecobee climates for one physical thermostat. Their device identities must match. HomeKit supplies normal controls; Ecobee contributes reported status and its own actions. Select optional entities only for the roles you want to expose.
mapping.title: Thermostat mapping

reconfigure.description: Add, edit, or remove thermostat mappings, read-only datapoints, and daily history mappings, then choose Save changes to apply the complete set. Saving reloads the integration. A request dispatched before reload may still take effect, while its pending confirmation is no longer retained.

datapoint_add.title: Add multi-source datapoint
datapoint_add.description: Select equivalent observations in preferred source order. Use one physical Ecobee item, or native weather aliases of the same station feed. These outputs are read-only. Changes are staged until Save changes.

data.name: Datapoint name
data.max_age_seconds: Default maximum report age (seconds; 0 disables expiry)
data.confirm_equivalence: Confirm these sources represent the same quantity, item, and time basis

data_description.name: Use a distinct name up to 64 characters. Editing the name preserves this datapoint’s stable identity.
data_description.kind: Select the quantity to centralize. Weather creates one native weather entity with current conditions and the selected source’s daily forecast. Configured membership keeps the complete source-local list and its profile/time context; it does not prove physical-set agreement, occupancy or Follow Me weighting.
data_description.semantic: For temperature, distinguish physical room, thermostat control/display and outdoor weather readings. For duration, distinguish elapsed time from minimum fan runtime per hour. Other quantities ignore this choice.
data_description.unit: Use the exact Home Assistant output unit for numeric quantities. Supported units are converted, never relabeled. Leave blank for whole weather, text, profile and configured membership.
data_description.time_basis: Current uses the latest eligible source report. Fixed interval requires source observation timestamps and the same explicit interval. Weather, membership and minimum fan runtime settings require Current.
data_description.interval_seconds: Required only for fixed interval. The selected source values must already represent this interval. Ecobee Unified does not aggregate or infer a daily runtime total.
data_description.max_age_seconds: Default maximum age for sources without an override. Zero keeps quiet event sources usable. Membership uses its source metadata clock where supplied; weather uses its provider forecast timestamp. A receipt or provider report is not proof of a new physical measurement.
data_description.fallback: Use the first usable source, then the second and optional third if enabled. Disabling fallback uses only the first source. This affects reads only and never changes thermostat command writers.
data_description.confirm_equivalence: Required to create this datapoint. Confirm that the selected observations represent the same quantity, item, and time basis. Matching physical identity alone cannot prove equivalent meaning.
data_description.primary_entity: Select the same physical thermostat or remote sensor, or weather aliases of the same native Ecobee station feed. Registry references survive renames; a different station or Ecobee connection requires a new datapoint.
data_description.primary_attribute: Leave blank for entity state or whole weather. For membership select active_sensors, profile_sensors or configured_sensor_names on a supported source. For a scalar weather reading, select the exact current field, such as temperature or humidity.
data_description.primary_timestamp_attribute: Required for ordinary interval values. Leave blank for weather, whose provider timestamp is read natively, and for membership using its native metadata clock. A current-profile state change does not establish member-list freshness.
data_description.primary_unit: Declare the unit only when the source attribute lacks unit metadata. A declaration cannot override contradictory native units.
data_description.secondary_entity: Select the same physical thermostat or remote sensor, or weather aliases of the same native Ecobee station feed. Registry references survive renames; a different station or Ecobee connection requires a new datapoint.
data_description.secondary_attribute: Leave blank for entity state or whole weather. For membership select active_sensors, profile_sensors or configured_sensor_names on a supported source. For a scalar weather reading, select the exact current field, such as temperature or humidity.
data_description.secondary_timestamp_attribute: Required for ordinary interval values. Leave blank for weather, whose provider timestamp is read natively, and for membership using its native metadata clock. A current-profile state change does not establish member-list freshness.
data_description.secondary_unit: Declare the unit only when the source attribute lacks unit metadata. A declaration cannot override contradictory native units.
data_description.tertiary_entity: Select the same physical thermostat or remote sensor, or weather aliases of the same native Ecobee station feed. Registry references survive renames; a different station or Ecobee connection requires a new datapoint.
data_description.tertiary_attribute: Leave blank for entity state or whole weather. For membership select active_sensors, profile_sensors or configured_sensor_names on a supported source. For a scalar weather reading, select the exact current field, such as temperature or humidity.
data_description.tertiary_timestamp_attribute: Required for ordinary interval values. Leave blank for weather, whose provider timestamp is read natively, and for membership using its native metadata clock. A current-profile state change does not establish member-list freshness.
data_description.tertiary_unit: Declare the unit only when the source attribute lacks unit metadata. A declaration cannot override contradictory native units.
data_description.primary_max_age_seconds: Leave blank to inherit the datapoint default. Zero explicitly disables age expiry; a positive value expires this source after that many seconds. Set a cutoff for a cloud source with a known reporting cadence while leaving a quiet local push source at zero. Native unavailable states still apply. Cadence is never inferred automatically.
data_description.secondary_max_age_seconds: Leave blank to inherit the datapoint default. Zero explicitly disables age expiry; a positive value expires this source after that many seconds. Set a cutoff for a cloud source with a known reporting cadence while leaving a quiet local push source at zero. Native unavailable states still apply. Cadence is never inferred automatically.
data_description.tertiary_max_age_seconds: Leave blank to inherit the datapoint default. Zero explicitly disables age expiry; a positive value expires this source after that many seconds. Set a cutoff for a cloud source with a known reporting cadence while leaving a quiet local push source at zero. Native unavailable states still apply. Cadence is never inferred automatically.

datapoint_edit_confirm.title: Edit multi-source datapoint
datapoint_edit_confirm.description: Preserve this datapoint's meaning and identity. Name, source priority, fallback, and freshness may change. A different quantity, meaning, time basis, or fixed interval length needs Add multi-source datapoint. Generic number/text sources must keep the same entity-and-attribute pairs; reordering is allowed. Changes are staged until Save changes.

data.name: Datapoint name
data.max_age_seconds: Default maximum report age (seconds; 0 disables expiry)
data.confirm_equivalence: Confirm these sources represent the same quantity, item, and time basis

data_description.name: Use a distinct name up to 64 characters. Renaming preserves this datapoint's stable identity and meaning.
data_description.kind: Keep the existing quantity type. Use Add multi-source datapoint for a different type so its observations have a new identity.
data_description.semantic: Keep the meaning used by this quantity. Physical room, control/display, and weather temperatures are distinct; elapsed duration and minimum fan runtime per hour are distinct. Use Add multi-source datapoint to change meaning. Other quantities ignore this choice.
data_description.unit: Temperature may change between °C, °F, and K; duration may change between s, min, h, and d. Meaning and time basis must stay the same. Keep all other output units unchanged, including Other numeric quantity. Confirm an allowed unit change.
data_description.time_basis: Keep the existing Current or Fixed observation interval choice. Use Add multi-source datapoint to change the time basis.
data_description.interval_seconds: For a fixed interval, keep its existing duration in seconds. A different interval length requires Add multi-source datapoint and a new identity. This field remains blank for Current observations.
data_description.max_age_seconds: Default maximum age for sources without an override. Zero keeps quiet event sources usable. Membership uses its source metadata clock where supplied; weather uses its provider forecast timestamp. A receipt or provider report is not proof of a new physical measurement.
data_description.fallback: Use the first usable source, then the second and optional third if enabled. Disabling fallback uses only the first source. This affects reads only and never changes thermostat command writers.
data_description.confirm_equivalence: Required for source changes, including reordering, and compatible unit or timestamp changes. Confirmation does not permit changes to physical item, weather feed, observation role, quantity, time basis, fixed interval length, or the generic number/text entity-and-attribute set. Name, fallback, and freshness changes alone do not need reconfirmation.
data_description.primary_entity: Select the same physical thermostat or remote sensor, or weather aliases of the same native Ecobee station feed. Registry references survive renames; a different station or Ecobee connection requires a new datapoint. Typed replacements must prove the same physical item and native observation role. Otherwise keep the bindings or add a new datapoint. For Other numeric quantity or Text status, keep the same complete set of entity-and-attribute pairs; reordering is allowed.
data_description.primary_attribute: Leave blank for entity state or whole weather. For membership select active_sensors, profile_sensors or configured_sensor_names on a supported source. For a scalar weather reading, select the exact current field, such as temperature or humidity.
data_description.primary_timestamp_attribute: Required for ordinary interval values. Leave blank for weather, whose provider timestamp is read natively, and for membership using its native metadata clock. A current-profile state change does not establish member-list freshness.
data_description.primary_unit: Declare the unit only when the source attribute lacks unit metadata. A declaration cannot override contradictory native units.
data_description.secondary_entity: Select the same physical thermostat or remote sensor, or weather aliases of the same native Ecobee station feed. Registry references survive renames; a different station or Ecobee connection requires a new datapoint. Typed replacements must prove the same physical item and native observation role. Otherwise keep the bindings or add a new datapoint. For Other numeric quantity or Text status, keep the same complete set of entity-and-attribute pairs; reordering is allowed.
data_description.secondary_attribute: Leave blank for entity state or whole weather. For membership select active_sensors, profile_sensors or configured_sensor_names on a supported source. For a scalar weather reading, select the exact current field, such as temperature or humidity.
data_description.secondary_timestamp_attribute: Required for ordinary interval values. Leave blank for weather, whose provider timestamp is read natively, and for membership using its native metadata clock. A current-profile state change does not establish member-list freshness.
data_description.secondary_unit: Declare the unit only when the source attribute lacks unit metadata. A declaration cannot override contradictory native units.
data_description.tertiary_entity: Select the same physical thermostat or remote sensor, or weather aliases of the same native Ecobee station feed. Registry references survive renames; a different station or Ecobee connection requires a new datapoint. Typed replacements must prove the same physical item and native observation role. Otherwise keep the bindings or add a new datapoint. For Other numeric quantity or Text status, keep the same complete set of entity-and-attribute pairs; reordering is allowed.
data_description.tertiary_attribute: Leave blank for entity state or whole weather. For membership select active_sensors, profile_sensors or configured_sensor_names on a supported source. For a scalar weather reading, select the exact current field, such as temperature or humidity.
data_description.tertiary_timestamp_attribute: Required for ordinary interval values. Leave blank for weather, whose provider timestamp is read natively, and for membership using its native metadata clock. A current-profile state change does not establish member-list freshness.
data_description.tertiary_unit: Declare the unit only when the source attribute lacks unit metadata. A declaration cannot override contradictory native units.
data_description.primary_max_age_seconds: Leave blank to inherit the datapoint default. Zero explicitly disables age expiry; a positive value expires this source after that many seconds. Set a cutoff for a cloud source with a known reporting cadence while leaving a quiet local push source at zero. Native unavailable states still apply. Cadence is never inferred automatically.
data_description.secondary_max_age_seconds: Leave blank to inherit the datapoint default. Zero explicitly disables age expiry; a positive value expires this source after that many seconds. Set a cutoff for a cloud source with a known reporting cadence while leaving a quiet local push source at zero. Native unavailable states still apply. Cadence is never inferred automatically.
data_description.tertiary_max_age_seconds: Leave blank to inherit the datapoint default. Zero explicitly disables age expiry; a positive value expires this source after that many seconds. Set a cutoff for a cloud source with a known reporting cadence while leaving a quiet local push source at zero. Native unavailable states still apply. Cadence is never inferred automatically.

historical_add.description: Group existing daily statistics for one physical thermostat, remote sensor, or shared weather feed. Historical identity continuity remains unknown. Changes are staged until Save changes; this daily view does not import or rewrite source history.

data.name: Daily history mapping name
data.anchor_ref: Entity identifying the item or weather feed

data.confirm_association: Confirm the sources belong to this item or weather feed and quantity

data_description.name: Use a distinct name for this daily history mapping. Renaming it preserves its stable identity.
data_description.quantity: Select the quantity to compare by day: temperature, humidity, battery level, carbon dioxide, AQI, VOC, weather temperature, or weather humidity. Weather sources are aliases of a shared feed; their association does not establish a physical weather sensor or independent measurements.
data_description.unit: Choose a compatible output unit. AQI 0–100 compares a scaled raw daily mean with a mean of provider-rounded samples; these methods are not interchangeable, and neither exactly reconstructs the other. VOC native values remain visible, but equivalent selection is blocked pending unit and calibration proof.
data_description.timezone: Defines each calendar day, including daylight saving changes. Defaults to the current Home Assistant time zone and must match that calendar and the captured sources.
data_description.anchor_ref: Select a registered sensor from Ecobee, HomeKit Device, Ecobee Unified, or Battery Notes, or a native Ecobee weather entity. Its identity or shared weather feed association must match the selected quantity. Weather association does not prove geography or independent measurement. Current association does not establish continuity throughout stored history.
data_description.primary_statistic: Required statistic ID and first preferred source for the same physical item or shared weather feed and quantity. An effective Beestat Statistics mapping may supply the association automatically. Explicitly confirm that the selected sources belong together.
data_description.secondary_statistic: Optional second statistic ID for the same physical item or shared weather feed and quantity. Ordered daily selection uses it only when the first source cannot supply that day.
data_description.tertiary_statistic: Optional third statistic ID for the same physical item or shared weather feed and quantity. Ordered daily selection uses it only when earlier sources cannot supply that day.
data_description.policy: Fixed source uses only the first statistic and leaves its gaps. Ordered daily selection chooses one whole eligible source for each day; it does not combine observations from different sources within a day.
data_description.accept_cross_method: Required for ordered daily selection across different methods, and for Beestat v3 complete-point versus legacy-day selection even with a fixed source. Acceptance does not make the methods equivalent or reconstruct missing samples.
data_description.confirm_association: Confirm that every statistic belongs to the selected physical item or shared weather feed and quantity. A current mapping or matching label cannot establish historical identity continuity. This view reads existing daily history and does not import or rewrite it.

command_unavailable.message: This integration instance has stopped, so this request was rejected before dispatch. Wait for it to load again. An earlier dispatched action may still take effect; inspect the thermostat before repeating it.

ecobee_command_failed.message: The Ecobee action returned an error. Inspect the thermostat and the native Ecobee integration before trying again; this error does not establish whether the requested change took effect. Ecobee Unified does not retry it.

ecobee_notification_failed.message: The notification service returned an error. Check the thermostat display and the native Ecobee notification source before resending. Delivery is not recorded in the thermostat command tracker, and no automatic resend occurs.

ecobee_notification_unavailable.message: Use a nonblank message and an enabled, available Ecobee notification entity on the mapped thermostat. Check the mapping’s device identity and that notify.send_message is available.

ecobee_writer_unavailable.message: The Ecobee action cannot be sent with the current source state. Check that the mapped climate has a fresh usable report, its device identity matches HomeKit, and the requested native service is available. Vacation requests also need a reported temperature unit and bounds.

homekit_command_failed.message: The HomeKit action returned an error. Inspect the thermostat and its HomeKit source before trying again; an error does not establish whether the requested change took effect. Ecobee Unified does not retry it.

homekit_writer_unavailable.message: The required local source cannot accept this request. Check its availability and thermostat association. For Current Mode or Clear Hold, verify that the entity has the intended role. This request is not rerouted through another source.

invalid_fan_runtime.message: Enter minimum fan runtime from 0 to 60 minutes in 5-minute steps.

invalid_humidity.message: Enter a whole-number humidity target within the limits currently advertised by the HomeKit thermostat. If those limits are missing, restore the source before setting humidity.

invalid_occupancy_modes.message: Supply true or false for at least one of auto_away and follow_me. Omit a field to leave that policy untouched.

invalid_sensor_selection.message: Choose 1–32 distinct Ecobee devices from the same integration entry as the mapped thermostat. Supply a comfort profile up to 64 characters, or omit it only while Ecobee reports a current climate_mode.

invalid_temperature.message: Enter a finite numeric target within the temperature limits currently exposed by the unified climate, using its displayed temperature unit.

invalid_temperature_range.message: Set the heating target at or below the cooling target.

invalid_vacation_name.message: Use a vacation name containing 1–12 characters after surrounding spaces are removed.

invalid_vacation_options.message: Choose auto or on for the vacation fan mode and a whole-number minimum fan runtime from 0 to 60 minutes.

invalid_vacation_period.message: Supply each date with its corresponding time, using YYYY-MM-DD and HH:MM:SS. When both start and end are supplied, the end must be later than the start.

invalid_vacation_temperature.message: Enter a finite numeric vacation temperature in the mapped Ecobee climate’s temperature unit.

invalid_vacation_temperature_bounds.message: Enter a vacation temperature between {minimum} and {maximum} {unit}, using the mapped Ecobee climate’s unit and limits.

invalid_vacation_temperature_range.message: Set the vacation heating temperature at or below its cooling temperature.

unsupported_command.message: This control is not currently exposed by the selected HomeKit source. Check the source’s availability and supported features before requesting it.

unsupported_fan_mode.message: Choose a fan mode from those currently offered by the unified climate’s HomeKit source.

unsupported_hvac_mode.message: Choose an HVAC mode from those currently offered by the unified climate’s HomeKit source.

unsupported_preset_mode.message: Choose an option currently advertised by the mapped HomeKit Current Mode select. Check that the select is available, belongs to this thermostat, and still has a valid preset role.

mapping_source_missing.description: For {mapping}, review these mapped sources: {source}. A source may be missing, disabled, associated with the wrong device, or incompatible with its assigned role. Open Ecobee Unified → Reconfigure to correct the mapping, or restore the native source. Missing sources are not replaced by matching names. For a retained missing optional source, clear its field to stop using it; otherwise restore the original registry entry. Device association alone does not prove that a generic button is Clear Hold.
mapping_source_missing.title: Check this thermostat mapping

error.invalid_timing: Use whole seconds: 300–7200 in 60-second steps for Ecobee freshness, and 300–1800 in 30-second steps for confirmation.
error.invalid_read_policy: Choose one of the supported source policies for each field.

data_description.confirmation_seconds: After a source call returns successfully, wait this long for matching reports: default 1800 seconds; range 300–1800 in 30-second steps. A match confirms reported settings, not room conditions or equipment performance. Expiry records unconfirmed without retrying. Resume, vacation, occupancy, and comfort-sensor actions record submission only; notifications do not use the tracker.
data_description.ecobee_stale_seconds: Exclude Ecobee climate and air-quality sources once their last Home Assistant report exceeds this age: default 1800 seconds; range 300–7200 in 60-second steps. Stale climate data cannot support reads or climate-based vendor actions. An unchanged report resets age without proving a new physical measurement. HomeKit sources have no age limit from this setting.
data_description.configure_read_policy: Continue to choose a thermostat and set source precedence for each reading. Timing changes and read policies are saved together after the final form. Command writers remain unchanged.

init.description: These settings control how Ecobee Unified interprets Home Assistant reports. They do not change source polling, thermostat schedules, or the source service-call timeout. Saving reloads the integration; cancellation or unload can end observation while an already-dispatched action still takes effect.
init.title: Freshness and command confirmation

data_description.mapping_id: The same field policies are available independently for every thermostat mapping.

read_policy.title: Thermostat read policy
read_policy.description: Choose source precedence for each reading. Normal thermostat commands still use their existing HomeKit writer; Ecobee-specific actions keep their existing writer. Source selection does not change schedules or polling.

data_description.hvac_mode: Prefer the chosen source when its value is usable; the fallback choices use the other source only when needed. Source availability, freshness, units, and validity still apply.
data_description.hvac_action: Choose which source owns the canonical action (heating, cooling, idle, or off). Detailed vendor equipment stages remain separate observations and may disagree due to source lag; read precedence does not reconcile their timestamps.
data_description.current_temperature: Choose the control-temperature source. HomeKit precision pairing remains subject to its agreement checks; a separate physical temperature measurement is not a substitute.
data_description.current_humidity: Prefer the chosen source when its value is usable; the fallback choices use the other source only when needed. Source availability, freshness, units, and validity still apply.
data_description.target_temperature: Prefer the chosen source when its value is usable; the fallback choices use the other source only when needed. Source availability, freshness, units, and validity still apply.
data_description.target_temperature_low: Prefer the chosen source when its value is usable; the fallback choices use the other source only when needed. Source availability, freshness, units, and validity still apply.
data_description.target_temperature_high: Prefer the chosen source when its value is usable; the fallback choices use the other source only when needed. Source availability, freshness, units, and validity still apply.
data_description.fan_mode: Prefer the chosen source when its value is usable; the fallback choices use the other source only when needed. Source availability, freshness, units, and validity still apply.
data_description.configure_another: Stage these choices and select another thermostat. All timing and policy changes save together when this option is cleared.

abort.configuration_changed: The saved configuration or options changed while this form was open. Reopen options to work from the current values.
abort.invalid_mapping_identity: The selected thermostat mapping is missing or repeated. No options were saved. Restore distinct mapping identities before continuing.
